**Body**:

Fourth and consolidating sweep of the day; supersedes all three earlier ones. All 10
sweeps ran. Every finding CATEGORY-classified per product-completion-first.md -- severity
ranks, it never gates fix-vs-defer.

THE ONE BLOCKING ITEM is PR #95, an inbound loom Gate-2 sync opened mid-session. It
merges cleanly and reverts today's security fix: measured on pr95, wx=0, actionDigest=0,
category-based-replace=0, team-memory=0. Merging as-is reintroduces silent audit-record
destruction and the read/write tier defeat. Recommending HOLD until Gate-1 ingests
proposals 71-72, because the other 98 files in that PR are not urgent while the two
reverted ones are the only shipped security fix in the repo -- and the merge-then-
re-apply alternative is a treadmill that gets forgotten on the third repetition.

A SECOND INSTANCE OF #79's CLASS, found by Sweep 9 rather than reasoned about: two
shipped commands cite `bin/lib/loom-links.mjs`, which sync-manifest.yaml:3141 fences
loom_only and purges from this lane. Worse than a dangling reference -- the Sweep-9 gate
was DESIGNED to emit N/A on the 30+ consumers, but the import throws before
isConfigured() is reached, so the fail-safe path is unreachable on exactly the audience
it was written for. Routed with #79; same root cause, one proposal.

FIXED INLINE (zero-tolerance Rule 1): the forest-ledger no-vanish gate was reporting
FAIL with two stranded workspace IDs (F5, F13) absent from the root ledger. Both rolled
up with their value-anchors intact; `--aggregate` now reports OK. That gate exists to
stop workstreams vanishing across the workspace-to-root boundary, and a permanently-red
gate is how a real strand gets waved through.

SURFACED, NOT SELF-DECIDED: 10 of 27 audit-fixture runners are RED on a clean tree --
measured by stashing, identical before and after today's changes, so pre-existing.
Recommending INVEST-NOW scoped to TRIAGE ONLY (classify loom-side vs local), not a
commitment to fix all 10 before knowing which are which.

Three INCREMENTAL items carry all four generalized Rule-1b conditions. The
deferred-quality backlog is empty, so no item is due a still-wanted revisit.

Sweep 7b's five stub-marker hits were checked rather than reported: all false positives
(the detectors contain the marker strings; one matched \uXXXX escape decoding). The one
real trace is a maintenance script emitting a TODO into GENERATED code -- filed
INCREMENTAL with its conditions.
